newsitem.title: ITALY: Gaddafi sees more Islamic attacks in U.S. - paper.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi sees more Islamic attacks in U.S. - paper.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi said in an interview published on Thursday that Islamic fundamentalists should not export their cause outside the Moslem world but predicted more attacks in the United States.
"The episodes of extremism we are seeing today are acts of pure folly," the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera quoted Gaddafi as saying.
"There are groups of terrorists who should be locked up in lunatic asylums rather than in jails," he said in the interview, which took place in Libya.

Gaddafi, whom the United States has accused of sponsoring terrorism, was asked his opinion of attacks attributed to Islamic fundamentalists and carried out in the Arab world as well as in Europe and the United States.
He said the groups, which he did not name, had misinterpreted the Koran.
"For example, I am absolutely against the use of weapons as I am opposed to transferring the Jihad (holy war) to Europe, as some of these groups would want," he said.
He said that justifying this would be tantamount to justifying European colonisation of Arab countries in the past.

Gaddafi said he was convinced that there would be other attacks in the United States, where radical Moslems have been convicted in the 1993 bombing in New York of the World Trade Centre, in which six people were killed.
"They hit a skyscraper and other targets and even if now they appear to be inactive, it is certain that they will strike again," he was quoted as saying.
Gaddafi said the United States and other Western countries should stay out of the Arab world.
He said Islamic fundamentalism had been fanned by what he called the West's "blind support" of Israel.

"My advice to America and the West is to distance themselves from the Arab world...maybe America is interested in possessing all of the oil in the world but it does not have this right," he was quoted as saying.
